newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Former S.Korean president Choi escorted to court.
newsitem.headline: Former S.Korean president Choi escorted to court.

text.p: South Korean prosecutors on Thursday escorted former president Choi Kyu-hah from his home to force him to appear in the appeals trial of his successors Roh Tae-woo and Chun Doo Hwan, state television reported.
Live television pictures showed Choi, caretaker president for 10 months following the assasination of strongman president Park Chung-hee in 1979, being whisked away in a limousine.
Smiling weakly and dressed in a dark business suit, Choi brushed past crowds of waiting reporters as he emerged from his home near central Seoul.
Choi repeatedly ignored prosecution demands to appear as a witness at the first trial of Chun and Roh, who were convicted on charges of bribery, mutiny and treason.
He insisted it would set a bad precedent for a former president to take the witness stand.

Prosecutors want to quesion Choi about the events surrounding a coup that thrust Chun to the presidency in 1980. They say Chun forced Choi from office as part of the putsch, but Chun maintains Choi asked him to step in to save the country from unrest.
